chunks: Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) mentioned one day good character and said: A servant of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) passed away, so he ordered that they dig a grave for him. They went and dug, and a rock appeared to them in the grave, so they were unable to dig. They came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said: O Messenger of Allah, we dug for so-and-so and a rock appeared to us, so we began to strike it until our pickaxes became notched. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: How is that? While he was of good character? Go back and dig. So they went back and Allah made it easy until they were able to bury him.
ai.seo_question: How does good character affect the ease of burial in the grave?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kitab al-Zuhd* illustrates the metaphysical impact of *husn al-khuluq* (good character) in Shia tradition, where moral excellence is believed to facilitate the physical ease of burial. The narrative highlights that the Prophet’s (SAWW) knowledge of the servant’s inner virtue allowed him to interpret the geological obstruction as a spiritual barrier, which was removed upon his command. This underscores the Shia emphasis on character as a tangible spiritual asset that influences one's transition to the afterlife.
